newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 29.

text.p: America Online Inc is expected to announce it will charge customers a flat-fee for unlimited access to the Internet, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.
- United Automobile Workers union might organize local strikes against General Motors Corp after it failed to agree on a new labor contract.
- Calenergy made a $1.23 billion bid for Britain's Northern Electric Plc.
- Germany's Henkel KGaA offered to buy 65 percent of Loctite Corp for $1.19 billion.
- Mercantile Bancorp and Mark Twain Bancshares agreed to merge in a $820 million stock deal.
- Revco D.S. Inc agreed to acquire Big B for about $380 million.
- McDonnell Douglas Corp will remain a minor player in commercial jet manufacturing.
- Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp announced plans for a cheaper personal computer.
- Food and Drug Administration gave Pfizer Inc approval to broaden the usage of its anti-depressant, Zoloft.
- Merrill Lynch said its president and chief operating officer would also become chairman and chief executive officer.
- A Union Bank of Switzerland unit and one of its officers were charged with fraud in Jersey, the Channel Islands.
- Fourteen U.S. states filed lawsuits alleging that Mazda Motor Corp's U.S. sales unit engaged in unfair and deceptive advertizing practices.
- Humana Inc is eliminating clauses in its physician contracts that doctors say might hinder their ability to communicate properly with patients.
- Salaries for chief executive officers at small, publicly-traded companies rose 17 percent last yeat, while the pay for those at bigger companies went up 12 percent.
- The U.S. bond market closed moderately lower in uneventful trading as it awaited important economic indicators.
- Investors are trying to find the company that will have the ultimate toy for the Christmas season. But some toy makers are not listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
